description: Calque Batch 1: Vietnamese 'đóng/tắt' leads learners to say 'close the TV' for an appliance. Rule en-calque-close-turn-off-appliance rewrites 'close the <whitelisted appliance>' to 'turn off the <appliance>'. Expectations encode the VERIFIED behaviour of correctWithTutorRules() on the engine WITH calque Batch 1 (MR !281) applied.
fp_risk_note: 'close' is correct for most physical objects, so the rule must stay scoped to the appliance whitelist. The negatives lock the boundary: (1) physically-closed objects ('door', 'window') keep 'close'; (2) lid-sense devices CUT from the whitelist ('laptop', 'computer') must NOT be rewritten; (3) head-noun boundary ('turn off the TV stand' — head noun 'stand') must not match; (4) already-correct 'turn off ...' is left alone. Positives cover the whitelisted appliances only.

negative.notes: Whitelist boundary: 'door' is physically closed; must keep 'close'.
Whitelist boundary: 'window' is physically closed; rule must not fire.
Locked regression guard (lid sense): 'laptop' CUT from the whitelist — you close a laptop lid; must not become 'turn off'.
Locked regression guard (lid sense): 'computer' cut from the whitelist; must not be rewritten.
Head-noun boundary: head noun is 'stand', not an appliance; must not match embedded 'TV'.
Already correct: 'turn off the TV' must not be re-touched.
